title: Strict Mode
html:
"use strict" opts a script or function into a safer dialect that turns silent mistakes into errors. ES modules and class bodies are strict automatically.

Turning it on

You rarely write it today: every ES module (import/export, .mjs, type="module") and every class body is strict whether or not the directive is present. Old-style scripts and CommonJS files are sloppy unless you opt in.

What changes

SituationSloppy modeStrict mode
Assign to undeclared variableCreates a globalReferenceError
this in a plain function callglobalThisundefined
Write to read-only / getter-only propertySilently ignoredTypeError
Add property to frozen / non-extensible objectSilently ignoredTypeError
delete a non-configurable propertyReturns falseTypeError
Duplicate parameter namesAllowedSyntaxError
with statementAllowedSyntaxError
Octal literal 0108SyntaxError (use 0o10)
arguments ↔ parametersLinked (aliasing)Independent
eval creates variables in the callerYesNo — own scope
Reserved future words (let, static, implements…)Usable as namesReserved

What is strict mode and why use it?

An opt-in restricted variant of JavaScript (ES5) that throws on silent errors (undeclared assignments, writes to read-only properties), makes this undefined in plain calls, forbids confusing features (with, duplicate params, octal literals) and enables engine optimisations. It is on by default in modules and classes.
